name: Goldilocks Principle of Optimal Stimulation
citation: Kirsh, D. et al. (2026). The Goldilocks Principle: Cross-modal prediction error optimization as the mechanistic basis for inverted-U preference curves in environmental psychology. CMR Working Paper, UCSD Cognitive Science.

constructs.description: The core mechanism: across all sensory modalities, there exists an intermediate level of prediction error that maximizes positive affect and engagement. Too little PE (fully predicted environment) produces boredom and allostatic underload; too much PE (unresolvable mismatch) produces anxiety, stress, and allostatic overload. The optimum corresponds to resolvable PE — stimulation that challenges the generative model enough to produce learning and dopaminergic reward but not so much as to overwhelm metabolic resources. This is the neural mechanism underlying Berlyne's (1971) Wundt curve and Kaplan & Kaplan's (1989) preference matrix.

The inverted-U is not merely a preference curve but reflects a metabolic constraint: the brain's predictive hierarchy operates within an energy budget (allostatic regulation via IC). Moderate PE is metabolically efficient — the generative model updates incrementally. Extreme PE (either direction) is metabolically costly: zero PE means the model is over-fitted and not learning (wasted maintenance cost); high PE means the model is failing and generating costly error-correction cascades. The optimal zone is where learning rate per metabolic unit is maximized.

While the mechanism is universal, the location of the optimum is domain-specific and calibrated by environmental statistics. Visual complexity: fractal D approx 1.3, corresponding to 1/f^beta power spectra with beta approx 2.6 (Taylor et al., 2011). Luminance contrast: global ratio 1:7 to 1:15 (Strother), CV 0.5-1.5 for aesthetic range. Thermal: adaptive neutral +/-1C for comfort zone, +/-1-3C for positive alliesthesia (de Dear & Brager, 1998). Acoustic: peak pleasantness 50-60 dB LAeq, natural sounds beta=+0.45 on pleasantness. Temporal variation: 0.01-2.0 cycles/min for light, optimal threshold density for architectural promenade sequences. Social: 3-5 simultaneous social modes (Dunbar saturation above 6).

At the moderate PE optimum, the neuromodulatory system generates positive reward signals: dopaminergic novelty reward (NM) from resolvable PE, serotonergic safety signaling from predictability within the comfort zone, and opioidergic pleasure from successful model updating. This triple reward convergence at moderate PE explains why the preference peak is robust across modalities — it is not merely the absence of negative affect but the active generation of positive affect through successful prediction.

The IE-DPT (Individual Experience / Dual Process Theory) framework explains why different individuals have different optima: prior expectations set the baseline against which PE is computed. An acoustician habituated to 85 dB finds 60 dB unremarkable; a librarian finds it distressing. A construction worker's thermal neutral is shifted by chronic outdoor exposure. Expertise compresses the PE curve (experts tolerate higher complexity before reaching overload) while novelty-seeking personality traits shift the optimum rightward. This person-dependence is irreducible — the same physical environment generates different PE profiles in different individuals.

schema_gaps: Olfactory Goldilocks zone not yet templated — scent intensity optima likely follow the same PE curve but no CMR template exists
Cross-modal interaction effects on zone boundaries incompletely specified — does thermal comfort shift the visual complexity optimum?
Developmental trajectory of optima unknown — do children have different Goldilocks zones than adults?
irreducible_residual.narrative: The irreducible residual of the Goldilocks Principle is the cross-modal universality claim itself: that all sensory channels optimize within the same PE efficiency framework, and that this optimization is a fundamental property of predictive brains operating under metabolic constraints. No single T1 framework captures this — PP explains the inverted-U shape, IC explains the metabolic constraint, NM explains the reward at optimum, and IE-DPT explains individual differences, but the claim that these four mechanisms interact to produce a UNIVERSAL cross-modal optimality principle is the Goldilocks Principle's distinctive contribution. This subsumes both Berlyne's optimal arousal theory (which described the curve without specifying the mechanism) and the Kaplan Preference Matrix (which specified environmental parameters without neural implementation). The domain-specific optima — fractal D 1.3, thermal neutral +/-1C, acoustic 50-60 dB, luminance CV 0.5-1.5 — are calibrated instances of a single underlying principle, not independent phenomena. This unification is a genuine theoretical contribution of the CMR system.

boundary_criteria.boundary_justification: GOLDILOCKS has cross-modal optimization unique to CMR synthesis (compositional_adequacy = INTERACTION_DEPENDENT with schema gaps in olfactory optima, cross-modal interactions, developmental trajectories). Prediction error optimization is constitutively relevant: intervening on stimulus complexity across any modality (visual fractal D, acoustic SPL, thermal range, luminance contrast) directly modulates preference and engagement following inverted-U curve. Design guidance is specific and calibrated: domain-specific optima (fractal D 1.3, thermal ±1°C, acoustic 50-60 dB, luminance CV 0.5-1.5) provide quantified stimulus parameters for each modality.

function_form.function_form: P(x) = exp(−(C(x) − C*)²/(2σ(ψ)²)); C* = optimal complexity

variables.C(x): Objective complexity measure (entropy, fractal dimension, etc.)

predictions: Peak preference at intermediate complexity across modalities
Experts have higher C* and narrower σ than novices

provenance.seminal_paper: Kasting, J.F., Whitmire, D.P., & Polivka, P.M. (1993). Habitable zones around main sequence stars. Icarus, 101(1), 108-128.
provenance.foundational_concept: Wundt, W. (1874). Grundzüge der physiologischen Psychologie (Foundations of Physiological Psychology). Engelmann.
provenance.predecessor: Wundt's inverted-U arousal curve (1874); Berlyne's optimal arousal theory (1971); Kaplan & Kaplan's complexity-preference matrix (1989); Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development (1978)
provenance.historical_context: The 'Goldilocks zone' term was coined by astronomer James Kasting et al. (1993) to describe circumstellar habitable regions. However, the underlying principle predates modern astronomy. Wundt (1874) first formalized the inverted-U relationship between stimulus intensity and preference. Berlyne (1971) developed optimal arousal theory applying this to all sensory modalities. Kaplan & Kaplan (1989) operationalized the principle with specific environmental variables (coherence, complexity, legibility, mystery). The principle gained metaphorical traction in cognitive development (Vygotsky's ZPD), flow theory (Csikszentmihalyi's challenge-skill balance), and astrobiology (habitability parameters). As a general principle of optimization across physical systems, it represents a unifying concept applicable to thermal comfort, acoustic preference, visual complexity, temporal dynamics, and social density.
key_milestones: 1874: Wundt formulates inverted-U relationship between stimulus intensity and affective response
1950s-1960s: Berlyne develops experimental psychology of optimal arousal
1971: Berlyne's Aesthetics and Psychobiology synthesizes arousal optimization across domains
1978: Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development (posthumously translated) formalizes developmental application
1989: Kaplan & Kaplan operationalize with environmental complexity metrics
1990: Csikszentmihalyi's Flow synthesizes challenge-skill balance as instance of Goldilocks principle
1993: Kasting et al. formalize 'habitable zone' concept in astrobiology
1990s-Present: Cross-domain application to thermal comfort (de Dear & Brager), visual complexity (Taylor fractals), acoustic preference
influenced_by: Rachel & Stephen Kaplan (1989, environmental preference metrics)
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi (1990, flow theory as instance of principle)
James Kasting et al. (1993, astronomical metaphor 'habitable zone')
Lev Vygotsky (Zone of Proximal Development, developmental instantiation)
provenance.current_status: foundational metaphor with active research across multiple disciplines (architecture, psychology, ecology, astrobiology, education)
provenance.verification_notes: Goldilocks term in astronomy (Kasting et al. 1993) verified via Icarus journal. Wundt (1874) foundation of inverted-U verified via history of psychology sources. Berlyne (1971) confirmed as key synthesis work. Kaplan & Kaplan (1989) verified. Historical trajectory from Wundt through Berlyne to modern applications confirmed via multiple academic sources. Note: this theory represents a synthesis/unification rather than single-origin foundational work.
